messages:
Maya: noticed a support ticket from VendorX that contains a blob that looks like a KMS ciphertext. can someone confirm scope?
Leo: can you paste the snippet (redact if needed)?
Maya: pasted minimal: `CiQA5...==|projects/redwood-prod/locations/us-east1/keyRings/partner-kr/cryptoKeys/ingest-key/cryptoKeyVersions/3`
Priya: that path is their KMS key (partner-owned) referencing our wrapped payloads? odd. do we surface partner keys in logs?
Sam: we log request metadata including caller-provided ciphertexts. looks like vendor sent their ticket with the full ciphertext attached.
Anika: is the ciphertext unwrapped anywhere on our side? i.e., any logs show plaintext?
Maya: quick grep across log retention (last 30d) shows only the ciphertext, no plaintext fields.
oncall-bot: incident-sev:low tagged. start checklist: rotation? audit? legal?
Leo: low severity for now but risk depends on what attacker could do with ciphertext. if key is partner-owned, rotating our keys won't help; we need partner to rotate and/or rewrap.
Priya: action plan suggestion: 1) confirm vendor key ownership & entitlements 2) ask vendor to rotate/rewrap and remove ticket history 3) restrict logs to strip ciphertexts going forward 4) audit RBAC for who can create KMS-wrapped payloads 5) legal/partner notification
Maya: I pinged VendorX security (ticket #VX-218) and requested an immediate deletion and rewrap. they replied: "we created the ticket by copy/paste, will scrub and rewrap with new key within 2 hours"
Sam: temporary mitigation: add a log processor rule to redact base64-looking blobs in support channel logs. i can push a rule to stage infra in ~15m.
Leo: also check Vault transit usage patterns. if any service used our transit key to produce ciphertext that ended up in vendor ticket, we need to rotate that transit key. Priya: which transit key?
Priya: vault/transit/redwood-ingest is used by partner-ingest lambda for payload sealing. Sam: that lambda pushes sealed blobs to partner endpoints. if vendor included sealed blob in ticket, it's probably fine, but rotate to be safe.
Anika: who can rotate Vault transit keys? we should avoid breaking in-flight consumers. recommend creating a new key version, update lambda to dual-write new ciphertexts, then phasing old.
Maya: proposed owners: Priya -> coordinate Vault transit rekey and partner request; Leo -> RBAC audit and log-redaction policy; Sam -> implement log redaction rule and dual-write change; Anika -> verify no plaintext exposure + runbook update; i'll own comms with VendorX and legal loop-in.
Priya: timeline estimate: create new transit key version and rollout dual-write in next 3 hours, monitor for errors for 24h, then rotate consumers to new key and deprecate old in 72h.
Leo: RBAC checklist: list all principals with create/update on transit keys and who can read wrapped ciphertexts in logs. i'll run `vault policy read` and `gcloud iam roles list` and share findings by EOD. sample commands:
```
# vault: show policies referencing transit
vault policy read partner-ingest || true
# gcloud: list iam bindings for key ring
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy ingest-key --location=us-east1 --keyring=partner-kr --project=vendorx-project
```
Sam: pushing redaction rule to staging now. rule: redact any base64 chunk > 80 chars in support channel message body. will also add a transform to hide `projects/*/cryptoKeys/*` patterns.
Anika: audit logging: enable DLP detection on outgoing support emails? may be overkill but worth recommending to VendorX. i'll draft suggested DLP config.
Maya: legal asked for quick summary. i sent the timeline + owners. they want confirmation vendor actually removed the ticket history.
VendorX (via ticket): "we scrubbed the ticket, rotated the key, rewrapped all affected payloads, and confirmed deletion of ticket body at 2026-03-21T14:03Z"
Maya: vendor confirmation received. can each owner ack next steps so we can close this thread?
Priya: ack — starting transit rekey dual-write now. will post status.
Leo: ack — starting RBAC audit, will flag any overly-broad roles and propose tighteners.
Sam: ack — redaction rule pushed to staging, will promote to prod after 30m smoke.
Anika: ack — DLP recommendations drafted and PR opened in vendor-runbook.
oncall-bot: incident-sev:monitor status updated.
Maya: thanks all. i'll follow up with a short postmortem template after 48h with findings and any runbook changes. :thumbsup:
